note.p: Godwin contacted four of the addresses in the flyleaf of his diary in the few days after Aaron Burr's departure, so they were clearly contacts Burr had given him (Godwin's diary vol xv: ‘David M Randolph 16 Francis-st, Golden-sq.’). David Meade Randolph was born in 1759 son of Richard and Mary. He was an officer in the Revolutionary war and a tobacco planter and slaveowner. In 1780 he married Mary Randolph his cousin, children William Beverley, Richard, James, Thomas Mann, Lavinia and David Meade jr (1784-1825). Mrs Randolph is famous for her cookbook, she stayed in Virginia while her husband was in England. In 1809 David Randolph patented a boot making machine, and in 1818 back in Virginia he was working on an improved form of cement.
